# Test vectors (generated by `scripts/gen_testvectors_md.py`; do not edit by hand)

Status: DRAFT, self-reviewed, not independently validated. Signature: public deterministic **TEST key**; SCITT registration **NOT DEMONSTRATED**.

## Wire format

`{"claim":C,"evidence":E,"kind":"p10-s1-instance-v0","profile":"p10-s1-toy-v0","spec":"sha256:<profile digest>","w0":A,"w1":B}` — a strict subset of RFC 8785 JCS (sorted ASCII keys, no whitespace, no trailing newline, values over `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`). Tokens — claim: `secondBit|firstBit`; evidence: `f{0,1}s{_,0,1}|inconsistent|outside`; world: `w00|w01|w10|w11|wOut`.

## What is real and what is not

* REAL, kernel-checked: `P10.Certs.P1.cert`, the reject theorems, decoder/round-trip theorems, SHA-256 FIPS vectors.
* REAL, script-checked: profile digest, source/manifest digests, JCS form and digests of the statement, COSE signature (test key).
* NOT DEMONSTRATED: SCITT registration/receipt, any Transparency Service, InstanceCommitment/closure/coverage, independent validation.

## Mutation suite

`python3 scripts/mutation_suite.py` — each case mutates a scratch copy and asserts the expected fail-closed verdict *and reason*. See the script's `CASES` table (statement-, source-, instance-, toolchain-, certificate- and runtime-level mutations, plus the pinned/unpinned `INFO` pair) and `THREAT_MODEL.md`.

## Benchmarks (build environment: 4 vCPU, 15 GB, Lean 4.33.0)

| what | measured |
|---|---|
| clean `lake build`, all modules (includes kernel decode + 4-block SHA-256 of P1) | ≈ 19 s, peak RSS ≈ 2.4 GB |
| `tests/Sha256Vectors.lean` (5 blocks) | ≈ 11 s |
| `tests/Decoder.lean` (14 vectors) | ≈ 2.5 s |
| checker-owned check of the P1 certificate | ≈ 1.2 s |
| canonical `verify.sh` without mutation suite | ≈ 1.5 min |
| ordinary `decide` on the 196-byte decode + canonical check | ≈ 1–2 s |

Design findings: (1) Lean 4.33 `String.toList` reduces slowly and pulls `propext`/`Classical.choice`, so bytes are `List Nat`; (2) `Nat.land/lor/xor` depend on `propext`, so SHA-256 bit operations are rebuilt from `/ % + *` (`Nat.rec`, direct `Nat.*` calls: ≈4× faster than instance-based operators); (3) wildcard patterns over enumeration types compile through `propext`-dependent lemmas, so matches list all constructors; (4) universal `decode ∘ encode = id` by brute-force `decide` over 175 instances timed out, so it is proved structurally. `native_decide` was never needed.
